rooms.16313: A rough lookout post squats among the pale trunks of the Light Forest, a platform of lashed poles raised a man's height above the ferns. Its ladder has rotted through at the third rung, and the brushwood screen that once hid it has gone brown and brittle. A cold firepit ringed with river stones sits beneath it, half buried in leaf litter. The only path is a narrow deer track leading north to a junction among the trees.
rooms.16317: The timber barricade comes to an end here against a jumble of boulders fallen from the mountain wall. Sharpened stakes, grey with age and lichen, lean outward over a ditch choked with nettles and dead leaves. Someone has wedged fresh logs into a gap near the bottom, the bark still on them. The trampled grass along the ditch leads back north to the barricade gate.
rooms.16326: From the inner side the barricade is a crude thing, its logs braced with slanting props and bound with rusted chain where the rope has rotted. A firing step of split planks runs along it, sagging in the middle where a support has given way. The stockade ends here against the rock of the mountain, and the packed earth turns west toward the black mouth of a great cave. The gate stands a short walk north along the wall of stakes.

16325.description: The mountain's rock leans out overhead in a great sooty lip, roofing a wide hollow at the mouth of the big cave. The air is warm and smells of coal smoke and hot iron, drifting from a heavy door of iron-banded planks set into the rock to the south. Cinders crunch underfoot, trodden into the stone floor by many boots. Grey light from the courtyard spills in from the north, while the rock face runs on west along the mountain wall and the end of the barricade lies east.

16320.description: A broad courtyard of beaten earth opens behind the barricade, rutted by cart wheels and pocked with puddles from the last rain. Grey cloud hangs low over it, snagged on the peaks of the mountain. The barricade gate stands close by to the east, and the dark mouth of the big cave yawns in the rock to the south. A broken water trough lies on its side near a hitching rail with no horses left to tie. The courtyard stretches on west, and to the north a path follows the foot of the mountain wall.

rooms.16321: Here the courtyard runs close under the mountain, whose grey cliffs crowd in on three sides and throw the ground into shadow for half the day. In the middle stands a weathered whipping post, its iron ring rusted fast. Over the turf roofs of the lean-tos the squat stone keep and its round tower stand against the rock, a catwalk girdling the top of the tower. Paths along the mountain wall lead north, south and west, and the open courtyard continues east.
rooms.16324: A strip of stony ground runs at the foot of the mountain wall, strewn with scree that has rattled down from the heights. Set into the cliff to the south is a squared doorway of heavy planks, the rock around it chiselled smooth by human hands. Thin grass and thistles grow along the base of the rock, and water seeps in dark streaks down its face. The wall leads east to the big cave and west to where the mountain bends, while the courtyard opens north.

16337.description: A tunnel has been hacked straight into the mountain here, its rock walls bearing the even scars of picks and chisels. The air is cold and damp, and drops of water fall from the low ceiling to spatter in shallow puddles on the floor. A door of heavy planks closes off the way north to the open air along the mountain wall. The passage runs west into darkness, where a stone staircase begins.

rooms.16323: The mountain wall turns sharply here, its cliff folding round a corner of the courtyard like the crook of an elbow. Rockfall has piled up in the angle, a slope of broken stone and boulders furred with green moss. An iron spike is driven deep into the cliff at head height, a frayed and rotten rope still knotted to it. Paths along the foot of the rock lead north and east, following the wall both ways.
rooms.16322: Ramshackle sheds lean against the foot of the mountain wall here, built of salvaged planks and roofed with bark and turf. Most stand empty, their doors hanging from leather hinges and their floors given over to dead leaves. A gutter scraped into the ground carries runoff from the cliff along the row. The courtyard opens to the east, and the path follows the rock north and south to the places where the mountain bends.
rooms.16330: Here the cliff swings round in a broad curve, and the mountain wall closes off a far corner of the fortress grounds. A spring trickles from a crack in the rock into a basin someone has chipped from the stone, overflowing into a muddy channel. Ferns and pale mushrooms crowd the damp ground below it, and the air is cool with spray. The path runs east along the mountain's foot and south along the other face of the wall.

16342.description: The cave opens into a smoky chamber of raw rock, its roof blackened by years of forge fire. A great stone forge built against the back of the cave still holds a bed of grey ash, and a battered anvil squats on a tree stump beside it. Empty iron hooks are driven into the rock where tongs and hammers once hung, and a quenching trough cut into the floor holds a skin of scummy water. The only way out is the heavy door to the north, back to the mouth of the big cave.

rooms.16347: A corridor of fitted grey stone runs through the keep here, its flagstones worn into a shallow trough by passing feet. In the floor a stairwell opens, and narrow stone steps lead down into the dark toward the bottom of a staircase. A cold draught rises from below, smelling of wet rock. The corridor continues north and south, lit only by a soot-stained arrow slit high in the wall.
rooms.16348: The corridor here is broader, and a strip of threadbare red carpet has been laid along the flagstones, its edges frayed into strings. In the west wall stands a stout oak door carved with a crude hawk, the only ornament for some distance. Iron sconces flank it, black with old soot and long since cold. The passage leads on north and south between the bare stone walls.
rooms.16349: The corridor turns a corner here, bending round a thick pillar of masonry. Water has found a way through the mortar overhead, and a slick of green slime runs down the pillar into a puddle on the floor. Someone has scratched a tally of days into the stone at shoulder height, row after row of patient marks. The way runs south and west.
rooms.16350: A long, straight stretch of corridor runs between bare walls of rough-dressed stone. Narrow arrow slits pierce one side, letting in thin blades of grey light and the smell of pine from the forest beyond. Dust lies thick along the edges of the floor, though a path through the middle has been kept clear by the tread of boots. The corridor leads east and west.
rooms.16351: A low iron-bound door is set deep in the south wall here, fitted with three heavy hasps and a keyhole the size of a thumb. The stone around its frame is scored with gouges, as if someone once tried to lever it open with a bar and gave up. The corridor carries on east and west, and the air hangs colder here than elsewhere in the keep.
rooms.16363: The treasury is a small vault of solid stone, its ceiling barely high enough to stand beneath. Empty strongboxes line the walls with their lids thrown back, and splintered shelves hang askew from their pegs. A pair of brass weighing scales is bolted to a stone bench, where the outcasts once measured out their shares of plunder. Scratches on the floor show where heavy chests were dragged out north through the door.
rooms.16352: Here the corridor narrows between two buttresses that jut from the walls, so that two people could barely pass abreast. Grooves for a portcullis run up both sides of the gap, though the gate itself is long gone and only a dark slot gapes in the ceiling where it once hung. Chips of fallen mortar crunch underfoot. The passage leads east and west.
rooms.16353: At this corner of the corridor a small niche in the wall holds a crude shrine, a stack of flat stones topped by a carved wooden figure with its face worn smooth by touching hands. Wax drippings have pooled and hardened at its foot in a pale crust. The air here smells faintly of tallow and damp. The passage continues east and south.
rooms.16354: The corridor runs straight between walls hung with tattered banners, their colours faded to a muddy brown and their devices too frayed to read. A long crack runs across the ceiling, and someone has propped it with a timber beam wedged against the floor. Water drips steadily from the crack into a hollow worn in the flagstones. The way leads north and south.
rooms.16355: A heavy door reinforced with iron straps stands in the west wall here, a narrow spy-hole cut through it at eye level. Benches of rough planks line the opposite side of the corridor, where sentries must once have sat out the long watches. The stone above the benches is scrawled with charcoal drawings of crude figures and the scores of old dice games. The corridor runs on north and south.
rooms.16356: The corridor bends here, the corner rounded off where years of shoulders have brushed the stone smooth. A drainage grate is set into the floor, and from somewhere far below comes the gurgle of running water. The air is close and smells of mould and old smoke. The passage leads north and east into the gloom.
rooms.16357: The corridor widens slightly where an open archway leads south into a long hall of beds. A sour smell of unwashed blankets and old straw drifts out from it. Wooden pegs line the wall beside the arch, where cloaks were once hung by men coming off watch. The passage continues east toward the heart of the keep and west round a corner.
rooms.16344: This is a crossing of passages at the heart of the keep, where four ways meet beneath a low vaulted ceiling. To the north the foot of a spiral staircase winds up into the tower, and to the south a wide doorway opens into a great dining hall that still smells of grease and woodsmoke. An iron chandelier hangs from a chain overhead, its candle cups empty. The corridor runs on east and west.
rooms.16343: The base of the tower is a cramped round chamber, its curved walls of heavy blocks rising into shadow. A spiral staircase of worn stone treads coils up around a central column, each step dished in the middle by countless feet. A rope rail threaded through iron rings follows the stair upward. A low doorway leads south back into the stone corridor.
rooms.16367: The spiral staircase ends at a small landing near the top of the tower, where the air is fresher and a breeze whistles through gaps in the stonework. A low door in the west wall opens onto the catwalk that rings the tower, and the creak of its planks carries in. The worn steps wind back down around their column into the gloom. Old rushes and stray feathers have gathered in the corners of the landing.
rooms.16368: A narrow catwalk of tarred planks clings to the outside of the tower, sheltered by a slanting roof of wooden shingles and guarded by a waist-high parapet of timber. Through the gaps between the parapet boards the courtyard lies far below, a muddy square of sheds and lean-tos. The doorway east leads back in to the head of the spiral staircase. The walkway curves away north and south around the flank of the tower.
rooms.16375: The catwalk turns a corner of the tower here, and the planks underfoot have warped so that they rock at every step. Grey cliffs loom close beyond the parapet, near enough that their cracks and ledges can be made out, streaked white by nesting birds. Wind moans under the eaves of the shingle roof. The walkway runs on east and south.
rooms.16374: Along this side of the tower the parapet has been patched with mismatched boards, some still bearing the flaking paint of an old cart or door. An arrow slit cut through the tower wall itself looks inward onto darkness. Beyond the timbers the mountain rises in a sheer grey face, its heights lost in drifting mist. The catwalk continues east and west.
rooms.16373: A corner of the catwalk juts out here on heavy timber brackets, giving a lookout a view two ways at once. A rusted iron brazier is bolted to the planks, its bowl full of rain-soaked ash and charred sticks. Over the parapet the forest spreads away beyond the barricade, a rolling sea of ancient grey trees. The walkway leads south and west around the tower.
rooms.16372: The catwalk runs straight along this flank of the tower, and from here the whole length of the timber barricade can be traced below, a jagged line of stakes between courtyard and forest. Several planks are missing, leaving gaps through which the drop is plain to see. Moss has crept along the shaded parapet rail and greened the shingles above. The way continues north and south.
rooms.16371: At this corner the shingle roof has partly fallen in, and broken shingles and a snapped rafter lie heaped across the planks. Rain has soaked the boards dark and soft, and they give alarmingly underfoot. Beyond the parapet the forest crowds up to the barricade, and somewhere past it the rush of a fast river can be heard. The catwalk leads north and west around the tower.
rooms.16370: On this side the catwalk passes beneath a row of iron hooks hammered into the tower wall, where wet cloaks or fresh game might once have been hung to dry. The parapet is studded with old arrowheads, broken off in the wood from some long-ago attack. Far below, the roofs of the courtyard sheds sag under moss and leaf mould. The walkway runs east and west.
rooms.16369: The catwalk rounds a corner of the tower, where a small bell hangs from a bracket under the eaves, green with age and missing its clapper. The parapet here leans outward, its posts loosened in their sockets, and a careless step could send a body over. The wind that slips under the roof smells of pine and damp stone. The walkway leads north and east.
rooms.16345: A doorway in the south wall of this corridor opens into a large room full of beds, from which comes a stale smell of sweat and mildew. The flagstones here are smeared with tracked-in mud, long dried to a pale crust. A heavy beam spans the ceiling, carved with initials and dates by bored hands. The corridor goes on east and west from the doorway.
rooms.16346: The corridor bends here, and the corner is darker than the rest, the nearest arrow slit having been blocked up with rubble and mortar. A cold draught creeps along the floor from the north, where a stair leads down out of the keep. Cobwebs hang thick in the angle of the ceiling, grey with dust. The passage runs north and west.
rooms.16361: Rows of narrow wooden cots fill this large room, their straw mattresses split and spilling onto the floor. A long table runs down the middle, scarred with knife marks and ringed with the stains of countless mugs. Wooden chests stand at the foot of some beds, their lids broken open and their contents long since taken. The only door leads north back to the corridor.
rooms.16362: The dining hall is vast for a fortress of outcasts, its high roof held up by blackened timber beams. Three long trestle tables run its length with benches on either side, enough to seat a small army, though most of the benches have been overturned. A great hearth yawns cold in one wall, the skull of a stag nailed above it. A door to the south leads into the kitchen, and the corridor lies north.
rooms.16365: The kitchen is low and smoky, its walls glazed brown with years of grease. A huge iron cauldron hangs from a chain over a fire pit in the middle of the floor, a crust of something burnt still clinging to its sides. Chopping blocks and a stone sink line the walls, and a smell of rancid fat hangs over everything. Doors lead north into the dining hall and west to a storage room.
rooms.16364: Shelves of rough planks line this cramped storage room from floor to ceiling, mostly bare now. Empty barrels stand stacked in a corner with their staves sprung, and rat-gnawed holes riddle the lowest shelves. Spilled grain has drifted into the corners like yellow dust. The air is dry and smells of old flour, and the door east leads back into the kitchen.
rooms.16360: This long, low hall was once a barracks, with sleeping pallets laid in rows along both walls beneath a vaulted ceiling. Many have been dragged together into heaps, as though the last sleepers here made a nest for warmth. A rusted brazier stands in the centre, its coals long dead, and soot has blackened the vault above it. The archway north leads back out to the stone corridor.
rooms.16359: The guard chamber is square and spartan, with a rack of empty weapon pegs along one wall and a table of scarred planks in the middle. A stout door bound in iron leads north into the armory, a heavy bar resting in brackets beside it. A hearth no bigger than a bread oven warms nothing now, its ashes cold and grey. The way east leads back out to the stone corridor.
rooms.16358: The grand armory is a long vaulted room lined with racks, stands and pegs enough to arm a war band, though nearly all of them stand empty now. A grinding wheel on a wooden frame sits in one corner, its stone worn into a deep groove. Straw training dummies slump on their poles at the far end, slashed open and spilling their stuffing. The door south leads back to the guard chamber.
rooms.16366: Yarick's Quarters are the finest rooms in the keep, which is not saying a great deal. A wide bed with carved posts stands against one wall, heaped with moth-eaten furs, and a writing desk beneath a narrow window is blotched with spilled ink. A bearskin rug covers the flagstones, and a tapestry of a hunting scene hangs crooked above the hearth. The door east leads back into the stone corridor.
rooms.16338: The church of the outcasts is a long chamber cut into the mountain, its walls left rough but its floor laid with smooth flagstones. Rows of crude benches made from split logs face an altar of a single great block of stone, stained dark at its centre. Above the altar a broken sword and a snapped chain hang crossed on the wall, the only creed the exiles kept. The way out is a passage east into the manmade tunnel.
rooms.16339: The Grieving Griffon is a tavern carved out of the rock, warm and low-ceilinged, with a bar of planks laid across upturned barrels. Above the bar hangs a painted sign of a griffon weeping into a tankard, its paint flaking away. Tables and stools are scattered about, many wobbling on uneven legs, and the floor is sticky with old ale. A door east leads out to the tunnel, and another in the west wall opens into a storage room.
rooms.16340: Casks and kegs fill this back room of the tavern, stacked against the rough rock in racks of split timber. Most have been tapped dry, and the sour reek of spilled ale and vinegar soaks the air. Cobwebs drape the highest racks, and the floor is stained dark around a split keg that leaked out its last long ago. The door east leads back into the Grieving Griffon.
rooms.16341: The hospital is a quiet chamber hollowed into the mountain, lined with narrow cots under coarse grey blankets. A stone table in the middle bears dark old stains and a row of iron rings for straps, and shelves above it hold bundles of dried herbs gone to dust. The smell of vinegar and bitter herbs still lingers in the cool air. A passage leads east to the manmade tunnel.

16321.description: The post is a stripped pine trunk sunk deep in the earth, its wood rubbed pale at the height of a man's wrists. The iron ring at its top has rusted solid, and the ground around its foot is trodden bare.

16349.description: Hundreds of short scratches run in neat bundles of five across the stone. The last row stops halfway, as though whoever kept count stopped caring or stopped being here.

16353.description: The wooden figure is no god anyone in Garathorm would know: a hooded traveller with a staff, carved by an unskilled hand. Its face has been rubbed away entirely by fingers seeking luck.

16338.description: The sword is snapped a hand's width above the hilt, and the chain beside it ends in a shackle that has been split open. Together they say plainly what the outcasts worshipped here: the breaking of whatever once held them.

16339.description: The griffon on the sign is painted with more feeling than skill, a great tear rolling down its beak into a foaming tankard. Beneath it someone has carved the words: drink, for we cannot go home.

16366.description: The tapestry shows riders in fine colours chasing a white stag through a forest, the work of some lord's household far from here. A long slash runs through the lead rider, and nobody has bothered to mend it.
